metadata.purpose: Plain-language wording for the 10 Profiler questions. Each question maps to a SHARE Wave 9 variable used by the K-means centroids. Choice values reproduce the SHARE coding so that downstream z-score standardisation (lib/profiler.ts) is correct.
metadata.audience: Anyone — designed to be answerable without specialist knowledge. Researchers and analysts looking at the technical labels can refer to data/centroids.json key_variables.

questions.prompt: How would you rate your overall health right now?
questions.helper: Self-rated health. SHARE uses a five-step scale where 1 is excellent and 5 is poor.

questions.prompt: Over the last month, how often have you felt sad, down, or in low spirits?
questions.helper: Approximation of the EURO-D depression scale (0–12). Pick the option that best describes the past four weeks.

questions.prompt: Do you need help with everyday tasks like cooking, taking medication, shopping, or managing money?
questions.helper: Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL): how many of these tasks need outside help (0 = fully independent, 7 = needs help with all).

questions.prompt: At the end of the month, how is your financial situation?
questions.helper: How easily the household makes ends meet. 1 = with great difficulty, 4 = easily.

questions.prompt: In the last 7 days, have you used the internet — for any reason (email, news, messaging, banking, shopping, video calls)?
questions.helper: Even a single use in the past week counts as Yes.

questions.prompt: How many people are in your close circle — family or friends you'd talk to about something important?
questions.helper: Size of the social network (1–7). Pick the closest option even if you're between two.

questions.prompt: Quick test: in the next 60 seconds, how many different animals can you name?
questions.helper: Verbal fluency. Type the count (most adults score between 10 and 25). If you don't want to test, type your best estimate.

questions.prompt: Looking at your life right now, how often do the things you do feel worthwhile and within your control?
questions.helper: CASP-12 quality of life (12–48). Higher means more autonomy, control, pleasure, and self-realisation.

questions.prompt: How often do you feel lonely?
questions.helper: UCLA loneliness short scale (3–9). Three states summarised here.

questions.prompt: Do you have things you look forward to or hope for in the coming years?
questions.helper: Whether the respondent reports forward-looking hope.
